content:
Apple's stock price reached a historic milestone during Tuesday's intraday trading, with its market capitalisation surpassing US$5 trillion for the first time, making it the second publicly listed company in history to achieve this feat.

Apple is the second company in history to reach a market capitalisation of US$5 trillion

Market capitalisation is calculated by multiplying a company's share price by its number of outstanding shares. As Apple continues its share buyback programme, the exact share price required to reach this milestone may vary.

This milestone comes after Apple previously hit a market cap of US$4.9 trillion and reclaimed the title of the world's most valuable company after swapping places with Nvidia. The two companies continue to take turns battling for the top spot. Apple has now joined Nvidia as the only two publicly listed companies globally to have surpassed this threshold.

Nvidia became the first company to reach a market capitalisation of US$5 trillion on 29 October 2025, driven by robust market demand for graphics processing units (GPUs) used to train and run generative artificial intelligence (AI) systems. Apple is the second company to reach a US$5 trillion market cap, a stark contrast to the pattern seen in the previous three rounds of the US$1 trillion market cap race.

Apple's market capitalisation has long been competing with Nvidia and Microsoft

Apple became the world's first publicly listed company to reach a market capitalisation of US$1 trillion on 2 August 2018, when its share price (ed.: AAPL) surpassed US$207.05; the stock subsequently underwent a split. The company took only about two years to double its market cap, becoming the first to reach US$2 trillion on 19 August 2020.

Less than 17 months later, Apple made history again, becoming the first company to touch a market capitalisation of US$3 trillion during intraday trading on 3 January 2022. AAPL's share price first recorded a closing market cap above US$3 trillion in June 2023.

This winning streak came to a halt at the next trillion-dollar mark. Apple first reached a market capitalisation of US$4 trillion on 28 October 2025, becoming the third company to hit this milestone after Nvidia and Microsoft. Nvidia was the first to reach the mark in July 2025, with Microsoft following suit later that same month.

Apple is undergoing a CEO transition

As always, this milestone is more symbolic than operationally significant. Nevertheless, a US$5 trillion market cap demonstrates Wall Street's extraordinary confidence in Apple and marks a fivefold increase in the company's market value over roughly eight years.

This milestone is achieved amid a CEO transition at Apple. Tim Cook will transition to the role of Executive Chairman of the Board on 1 September, with John Ternus taking over as Apple's CEO.

Apple will release its latest quarterly results on 30 July.
